# eon_finding_exclusion (Resource)

Manages a finding exclusion that stops one detector from reporting findings for matching files, tables, or databases, on one resource or on every resource in the account. An exclusion applies to scans that start after it is created or updated.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Suppress malware findings for a cache directory on one EC2 instance
resource "eon_finding_exclusion" "malware_cache" {
  scope                = "RESOURCE"
  provider_resource_id = "i-0abc123def4567890"
  value                = "/var/cache"
  type                 = "PATH"
  detector             = "MALWARE"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `detector` (String) Detector whose findings the exclusion suppresses. Supported values: `RANSOMWARE_BEHAVIOR`, `DATA_ANOMALY`, `MALWARE`.
- `scope` (String) Where the exclusion applies. `RESOURCE` applies it to the resource named by `provider_resource_id`. `ACCOUNT` applies it to every resource in the account. Supported values: `RESOURCE`, `ACCOUNT`.
- `type` (String) What the exclusion matches. Supported values: `PATH`, `TABLE`, `DATABASE`.
- `value` (String) What the exclusion matches. For `PATH`, every file whose path starts with this value. Linux paths are compared case-sensitively. Windows paths are compared as the backup stores them, which is currently lowercase, so write Windows prefixes in lowercase (for example `c:/users/app/cache`). For `TABLE` or `DATABASE`, the exact table or database name.

### Optional

- `provider_resource_id` (String) Cloud provider ID of the resource the exclusion applies to, such as an EC2 instance ID or an Azure resource ID. Required when `scope` is `RESOURCE`, and must be omitted when `scope` is `ACCOUNT`.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Finding exclusion ID.
- `updated_at` (String) When the exclusion was created or last updated.
